title: Pediatric Choking: Emergency Recognition & Relief Protocol
summary: A comprehensive, step-by-step clinical guide to recognizing and treating choking in infants and children, following the UK 2010 Algorithm. This resource covers maneuvers for conscious and unconscious victims, including specific techniques for back blows, thrusts, and CPR.

branches: Immediate coughing reaction to expel foreign body
Most events occur during play or eating
Risk: Rapid asphyxiation if cough is absent/ineffective

sections.title: Differential Diagnosis: Suspect Foreign Body IF:
content: 1. The onset was very sudden
2. There are no other signs of illness
3. Clues present: History of eating or playing with small items immediately prior to symptoms
Note: Similar signs/symptoms can be laryngitis or epiglottitis (require different management)

rows: Effective Coughing
No external manoeuvre. Encourage coughing and monitor continuously.
Ineffective/Absent Coughing
Shout for help immediately. Determine conscious level. Active intervention required.

sections.title: Conscious Child: Back Blows (Infant vs. Child)
content: Determine conscious level: If still conscious but cough is absent/ineffective, give back blows.
INFANT: Support head-downwards, prone position across rescuer's lap.
INFANT: Support head by thumb at angle of lower jaw and fingers at the other side. Do NOT compress soft tissues under jaw.
CHILD > 1 YR: Position head down (across lap or forward-leaning position supported from behind).
ACTION: Deliver up to 5 sharp back blows with the heel of one hand between shoulder blades.
GOAL: Relieve obstruction with each blow rather than giving all 5.

sections.title: Conscious Child: Thrusts (When Back Blows Fail)

rows: Positioning
Head-downwards supine position on arm/thigh; encircle occiput with hand.
Stand or kneel behind; arms under child's arms; encircle torso.
Landmark
Lower sternum (finger's breadth above xiphisternum).
Between umbilicus and xiphisternum.
Technique
Sharp chest compressions delivered at a slower rate.
Clench fist, grasp with other hand; pull sharply inwards and upwards.
Limit
Up to 5 thrusts (relieve with each thrust).
Repeat up to 4 more times (total 5).
Contraindication
Do NOT use Abdominal Thrusts (Heimlich) for infants.
Do NOT apply pressure to xiphoid process or lower rib cage.

sections.title: Following Thrusts: Reassessment
content: If object not expelled and victim conscious: Continue sequence of back blows and chest/abdominal thrusts.
Call or send for help if not available. Do not leave the child.
If object expelled: Assess clinical condition. Part may remain in respiratory tract.
If doubt: Seek medical assistance.

sections.title: Unconscious Child Management
content: Place on firm, flat surface.
Call/send for help (Do not leave child).
Airway: Open mouth and look for object.
Remove ONLY if visible with a single finger sweep.
Attempt 5 rescue breaths (Reposition head if chest doesn't rise).
Proceed to CPR immediately after breaths if no response.

sections.title: DANGER: Airway Opening Warning
content: Do NOT attempt blind or repeated finger sweeps.
These can impact the object more deeply into the pharynx and cause injury.

content.explanation: Rate: 100-120 min-1. Ratio: 15 compressions to 2 breaths. Depth: 1/3 of chest depth.

sections.title: CPR Execution Protocol (Step 7B)
content: Check pulse: If no signs of life (unless pulse >60 min-1 is certain within 10s), start chest compression.
Combine rescue breathing and chest compression.
Compress lower half of sternum (avoiding upper abdomen).
Locate xiphisternum: compress sternum one finger’s breadth above the angle where ribs join.
Release pressure completely between compressions.
Perform for ~1 min before summoning EMS (if alone).
If obstruction relieved: Check airway, deliver rescue breaths if not breathing, assess for life, continue CPR if needed.
If breathing/conscious: Place in safe side-lying (recovery) position and monitor.

rows: Infant
Compress sternum with tips of two fingers.
Encircling technique: Thumbs side-by-side on sternum; fingers encircle rib cage supporting the back.
Child Over 1 Year
Heel of one hand over lower sternum; lift fingers off ribs. Arm straight, position vertically above chest.
For larger children/small rescuers: Use both hands with fingers interlocked.
